newsitem.title: USA: Duke, CP&L say storm damage slight.
newsitem.headline: Duke, CP&L say storm damage slight.

text.p: Ice and snow piled up in North Carolina overnight, making roads treacherous and snapping power lines snared in ice-laden tree limbs.
Some 10,000 customers of Duke Power Co. remain without electricity, most of them in western North Carolina, according to spokesman Randy Wheeless.
"(The damage) is not too severe," Wheeless told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Many schools were closed throughout North Carolina, and hundreds of accidents were reported to state highway patrol offices throughout central North Carolina. None were fatal.
"About 10,000 customers are without power in the two Carolinas and the hardest hit area was Charlotte with about 5,500 customers without power," Wheeless said.
He added that fallen trees and tree limbs tore down power lines overnight, and that at the height of the power outage some 18,000 customers did not have power.
"We're looking to have everyone back up by today," he said. "This is minimal."
A Carolina Power & Light Co. spokeswoman said its customers in central North Carolina were only slightly impacted by the storm, noting 4,000 outages at peak.
